overview:
California's 31st District leans Democratic by eight points, and incumbent Gil Cisneros enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage. He has raised about $830,000 to Eric Ching's $97,000, holds a cash-on-hand edge of more than twenty to one, and is the only candidate drawing outside support. Ching, running with little money in the bank, has not shown the resources to contest the seat seriously.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals: the Democratic lean, Cisneros's incumbency, and a national environment favoring Democrats. Prediction markets price Cisneros at roughly 95 percent to win. The forecast rates the race Safe D, with an expected margin near nineteen points; the main caveat is that no polling exists to test those fundamentals directly.
